macro.regime: AI-capex melt-up colliding with a hawkish Fed hike cycle
macro.narrative: Hot October CPI (core +0.3% m/m) triggered a decisive hawkish repricing -- Fed's Waller and Logan both publicly floated a December hike (Waller explicitly said a 50bp move 'should be considered'), and CME-implied odds of a December hike now sit near 88-96% with essentially nothing priced for a hold or cut; the 10Y yield jumped to roughly 4.9-5.0% (2Y ~4.75-4.80%, a steepening curve) and DXY firmed to ~102.3. Equities shrugged this off violently on Wed 11 Nov (S&P +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%, VIX -10.1%) because CoreWeave's blowout earnings and $132.5B backlog reignited the AI-capex trade, adding over $500B of market cap across chips/memory/power names in a single session and reconfirming hyperscaler 2027 capex guidance toward a combined >$1T (Google $284.8B, Amazon $256.5B, Microsoft $207.6B, Meta $185.6B). Gold/silver's divergence from equities is a real-yield story, not risk-off: GLD -1.13%/GC -0.89% reflect real 10Y yields near 2.6% (historically a heavy gold headwind) plus the firming dollar, while SLV's relative resilience (+0.37%) points to industrial/AI-power demand partly offsetting the real-rate drag. Credit is bifurcated (aggregate HY OAS a benign ~334bp, but CCC-tier OAS at the 99th percentile since Oct-2023) and China's credit impulse is soft (Sept new loans beat only on government bond issuance, M2 at an 18-month low), so the regime is less a clean goldilocks than a fragile, AI-capex-subsidized risk appetite sitting on top of a genuinely hawkish rate path. Separately, China's rare-earth export-control suspension (agreed at the Trump-Xi meeting) expired 10 Nov with no formal renewal confirmed -- the live catalyst behind this week's rare-earth-basket strength.
